analysis.text: M: Welcome to "Business Matters". Today we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work. Hi, Lucy. Many of us never seem to get promoted. Why is that? And what can we do about it? 男：欢迎来到《Business Matters》。今天我们邀请了职业发展顾问 Lucy Williams 来谈谈 如何在职场上取得进步。嗨，Lucy。很多人似乎一直得不到晋升。为什么会这样？我们能做 些什么？

questions.stem: What does the woman say is one mistake people make?
questions.stemZh: 女士说人们会犯的一个错误是什么？
questions.answerText: To limit communication only to their superiors.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses. It's important to expand your network and include your co-workers. 女：人们犯的一个错误是只跟老板沟通。重要的是拓展人脉，把同事也包括进来。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者直接应答 + 关键信息 “One mistake...”。男人在 P1 末尾问 “Why is that? And what can we do about it?”，女人在 P2 直接以 “One mistake people make is...” 作答， One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses. 就是答 案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: limit communication only to their bosses. ↔To limit communication only to their superiors. 同义替换：bosses = superiors

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 To mix and interact with peers within the organization. 中的 mix/interact with peers 是女人后面建议 “expand your network and include your co-workers” 的同义改写，但 题干问的是 “mistake”，这是正确做法而非错误。 借用原文：expand your network and include your co-workers. B) 张冠李戴 To restrict their connections exclusively to colleagues. 盗用了 include your co- workers. 中的 co-workers（colleagues 同义）与 communication/connections 概念， 但把对象从 “bosses” 换成了 “colleagues”，与原文相反。 借用原文：include your co-workers. D) To underestimate their role in the company. 中的 underestimate 出现在 It's important not to underestimate your colleagues.，但这是第4段关于“不要低估同事”的内容，与第2 段的 “mistake” 不是同一个。 借用原文：It's important not to underestimate your colleagues.

questions.stem: What does the woman advise people to do in their work?
questions.stemZh: 女士建议人们在工作中做什么？

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: Yeah, it's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time. And these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve. 女：是的，你最好确保自己投入的是高质量时间，而不是单纯的大量时间。并且这些努力可 以通过我们取得的成果轻易体现出来。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 建议句 it's better to... + 取舍 instead of。男人在 P5 提出 “working hard... staying late” 的困惑，女人在 P8 用 “it's better to...” 给出建议，并用 “instead of” 把 “quality time” 与 “quantity of time” 对立，答案落在 quality time 上。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: putting in quality time ↔Put in quality time. 直接提取核心动作短语

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 Connect with managers. 对应 limit communication only to their bosses. 中的 bosses，但女人在第2段明确说“只跟老板沟通”是错误，不是建议。 借用原文：limit communication only to their bosses. C) 原词陷阱 Make greater efforts. 对应男人在 working hard creates a good impression 中的 working hard，但女人随后否定 “constantly staying late just to show committed”，说 明她不赞成单纯更努力。 借用原文：working hard creates a good impression D) 偷换概念 Demonstrate final results. 来自 these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.，但原文中 results 是 quality time 的自然结果，不是女人直接建议去 做的事。 借用原文：these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.

questions.stem: Why does the man say one should not act like a know-it-all?
questions.stemZh: 男士为什么说一个人不应该表现得无所不知？

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: M: But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all, otherwise you'll appear arrogant. 男：但不用说，你不应该表现得像个万事通，否则你会显得傲慢。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果连接词 otherwise 后的结果。男人在 P11 用 “otherwise you'll appear arrogant” 直 接给出 “不要表现得像 know-it-all” 的原因/后果，otherwise you'll appear arrogant. 是答 案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: you'll appear arrogant. ↔To avoid appearing arrogant. 条件-目的转换：otherwise you'll appear arrogant → to avoid appearing arrogant

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 To show their genius. 来自 you'll get a lot of time later on to show your genius.，但 那是 Lucy 对 “be humble” 的补充说明，不是 “不要 know-it-all” 的原因。 借用原文：you'll get a lot of time later on to show your genius. B) 原词陷阱 To gain due respect. 来自 help them out to gain their respect and trust.，但这是关于 帮助同事的建议，与 know-it-all 无关。 借用原文：help them out to gain their respect and trust. C) 未提及 To guard against humiliation. 中的 humiliation 在录音中完全没有出现，是利用 arrogant 的负面情感色彩编造的近义干扰。 1 W: I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities. From what I recall, the presentation consists of five parts, not including the introduction and conclusion. That would mean altogether, we need to allocate seven parts between the two of us. W: 我觉得我们首先需要决定如何分配演示的任务。据我所记得，这次演示由五个部分组成，不包括开头 和结尾。也就是说，我们总共需要在我们两个人之间分配七个部分。 2 M: So, we have the abstract, background research, the project design, the results and the discussion portions. As the abstract section only applies to the article, we needn't include it in the presentation. How would you suggest we dole out the rest? M: 所以，我们有摘要、背景研究、项目设计、结果和讨论这几个部分。由于摘要部分只适用于文章，我 们不必把它包括在演示中。你建议我们如何分配剩下的部分？ 3 W: How do you feel about handling the background bit? In this way, we can both discuss the part of the project that we devoted most of our time to. W: 你觉得由你来负责背景研究部分怎么样？这样一来，我们就都可以讲述自己投入最多时间的项目部 分了。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 4 M: Hold on a minute. You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation? The background research which was so meticulous took more than a month. M: 等一下。你是想让我这个承担了大部分任务的人，再负责演示的大部分内容？那份一丝不苟的背景研 究花了一个多月的时间。 5 W: OK. OK. I get it. Quit your moaning. I appreciate the rigorous work ethic you applied to the research, but not the sarcasm that comes up every time I mention it. What do you think would be a fair arrangement? W: 好了，好了。我明白了。别再抱怨了。我认可你在研究中所表现出的严谨工作态度，但不欣赏每次我 提到这件事时你表现出的讽刺。你觉得怎样分配才公平？ 6 M: I think the best arrangement would be to split the research into two parts: before-1980 and afterward. I would take the before-portion and you would be assigned the after-1980, leaving the project and results. I volunteer to describe the project. But as I struggled a bit with the statistics in the results section, how about you handling that? M: 我觉得最好的安排是把研究分成两部分：1980年以前和之后。我负责1980年以前的部分，你负责 1980年以后的部分，项目设计和结果部分则另行分配。我自愿介绍项目设计。不过，我在结果部分的统 计数据方面有些吃力，你来负责那一部分怎么样？ 7 W: That's agreeable to me. I propose we both handle the discussion section in parts along with the question and answer afterward, leaving only the introduction and conclusion. W: 我觉得这样可以。我提议我们分段负责讨论部分，之后的问答环节也由我们共同完成，这样就只剩下 开头和结尾了。 8 M: I will take responsibility for the conclusion and put you in charge of the introduction. This will make it so that we alternate presenting, so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience. M: 我来负责结尾，你来负责开头。这样我们就可以交替进行演示，避免让听众觉得单调。

questions.stem: What can makeup do according to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland?
questions.stemZh: 根据苏格兰斯特灵大学的一项最新研究，化妆能起到什么作用？
questions.answerText: Alter others' perceptions of the wearer.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Makeup can do more than just change your appearance—it can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse. According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious, positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat. 化妆不仅能改变你的外貌——它还能改变他人对你的看法，无论好坏。根据苏格兰斯特林大 学的新研究，尽管男性和女性都认为化妆的女性地位更高，但男性将化妆与有声望的积极品 质联系在一起，而女性则认为化妆的其他女性更具主导性且是一种潜在威胁。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 主题句 + 研究来源句。答案信号来自段落开头的主题句 'Makeup can do more than just change your appearance—it can also alter others' perceptions of you'，其中 'it can also alter others' perceptions of you' 直接回应题干 'What can makeup do'；随后 'According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland' 进一步给出具 体研究发现。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: alter others' perceptions of you ↔Alter others' perceptions of the wearer. 同义改写：第二人称转第三人称

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 答非所问 选项 B 的 admiration 看似和 gain others' trust and admiration 有关，但该句是作者基 于研究给出的应用建议，并非题干所问的 'new research from the University of Stirling' 的直接结论，属于答非所问。 借用原文：gain others' trust and admiration C) 未提及选项 C 的 confidence 在全部四段录音中均无对应内容，属于未提及。 D) 原词陷阱 选项 D 盗用原文原词 change your appearance，但原文说 'Makeup can do more than just change your appearance'，言下之意 '改变外貌' 只是常识层面，新研究真正关注的是 'more than' 之后的 'alter others' perceptions'；选项把 'more than just' 之前的旧信息拿 来当答案，答非所问。 借用原文：change your appearance

questions.stem: How did both men and women rate the faces with cosmetics in the new research?
questions.stemZh: 在这项最新研究中，男性和女性如何评价化妆后的面孔？

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive, but only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige. 研究显示，男性和女性都认为化妆后的脸更具吸引力，但只有女性认为化妆后的脸更具主导 性，只有男性认为化妆后的脸更有声望。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 对比结构 'both...but only...while only...'。答案信号是对比结构 'men and women both... but only women... while only men...'，题干问 'both men and women'，因此答 案落在 'both' 引导的分句里，即 'more attractive'。

analysis.label: 替换

questions.stem: The proposals __(26)__ caps on rent increases

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: 复数主语 proposals 之后缺谓语，需动词原形（一般现在时）

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: impose caps/limits on 是政策语域的固定搭配，「对……设限」 The proposals __(26)__ caps on rent increases, preventing landlords in the state from raising rent more than the rate of inflation in most cases.——提案「对租金涨幅设上 限」，呼应首段 put some limits on ever-increasing rent prices，impose caps on 与 put limits on 是同义改写，这正是六级最爱考的「换说法不换意思」。

analysis.label: 竞争词
analysis.text: M) presume presume 意为「假定」，与 caps 不构成搭配且逻辑相反 presume 是「假定、推测」，presume caps 不是英语搭配；且提案是「实际设限」而非「假定 存在上限」，代入后与后半句 preventing landlords…（实际阻止房东涨租）矛盾。

analysis.label: 易错
analysis.text: 最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— presume 与 impose 同为原形动词，「提案假定上限」粗 读似乎也通。The proposals __(26)__ caps on rent increases 中 presume 形态合格，且 考生若只认识 presume 不认识 impose，容易用「熟悉的词」填。防坑：盯住宾语搭配 ——caps/limits 的舞伴是 impose（impose caps on），presume 后接的是「事实从 句」；再回看首段 put some limits on ever-increasing rent prices，同义改写的锚点直接 指向 impose。

questions.stem: There are exceptions for buildings less than 10 years old, public housing, improvements beyond maintenance, and a hardship __(27)__.

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: 不定冠词 a + 名词作定语的 hardship 之后，需单数可数名词

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: hardship exemption「困难豁免」是政策文本的固定说法，且与 exceptions 同义呼应 There are exceptions for buildings less than 10 years old, public housing, improvements beyond maintenance, and a hardship __(27)__.——列举的都是「不适用 该限制的豁免情形」，a hardship exemption（因困难而获得的豁免）与句首 exceptions 同义复现，政策语域用词精准。

analysis.label: 竞争词
analysis.text: C) constituent constituent「选民」不能与 hardship 构成政策豁免概念 a hardship constituent 字面上是「一位困难的选民」，但本句列举的是例外「情形/类别」 （建筑、公屋、改良工程），不是人；且选民不属于租金管制条例的豁免条款范畴，语义场 不合。 N) rehabilitation rehabilitation 意为「康复/修复」，与 hardship 搭配不成立 hardship rehabilitation（困难修复）不是英语里的政策术语；rehabilitation 多指罪犯改造、 病人康复或建筑翻修，与「豁免条款」的语境无关。

questions.stem: every $100 in rent increase is __(28)__ to a 9% rise in homelessness

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: be 动词 is 之后、介词 to 之前，需过去分词构成 be done 表语结构

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: be correlated to 是固定搭配，意为「与……相关」，严丝合缝 研究语境 researchers at the U.S. Government Accountability Office estimated that every $100 in rent increase is __(28)__ to a 9% rise in homelessness：租金每涨 100 美 元「对应/关联」无家可归率上升 9%——这正是相关性表述，be correlated to/with 是六 级阅读与选词填空的高频固定搭配，语义与搭配双契合。

analysis.label: 竞争词
analysis.text: G) enacted enact 的搭配对象是法律而非数据关系 enacted 意为「颁布（法律）」，其主语应是立法机构、宾语是法案；「租金上涨被颁布成无家 可归率上升 9%」语义不通，且 enact 不与 to 构成表语搭配。 K) notified notify 的对象必须是人 notify sb of/that… 意为「通知某人」，被通知方是人；这里主语是 every $100 in rent increase（物），「租金上涨被通知给无家可归率」不成立，也不与 to 搭配。

questions.stem: telling the story of a __(29)__ struggling to live in the community

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: 不定冠词 a 之后、分词短语 struggling… 之前，需单数可数名词指人

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: 议员讲「选民」的艰难故事，身份与语境严丝合缝 Representative Alex Ramel explained why he thought that this kind of legislation was so important, telling the story of a __(29)__ struggling to live in the community. ——说话者是 Representative（众议员），议员为自己的立法辩护时讲的是「选区选民」 的故事；constituent 正是「（选区的）选民」，且下一段 he made the decision to introduce the legislation while talking to a young man in Bellingham 的 a young man 就是这个 constituent 的具体化。

analysis.label: 竞争词
analysis.text: N) rehabilitation rehabilitation 是抽象事物名词，不能「挣扎着生活」 rehabilitation（康复/修复）是物不是人，无法充当 struggling to live 的逻辑主语；「一个挣 扎着住在社区里的康复」语义荒谬，直接排除。

questions.stem: Ramel pointed out the __(30)__ effect of double-digit rent increases

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: 定冠词 the 与名词 effect 之间，需形容词作定语

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: devastating effect 是高频搭配，且与「两位数涨幅」的负面语境吻合 上下文 Ramel pointed out the __(30)__ effect of double-digit rent increases 与 Rent increases have an even more detrimental effect on some demographic groups 呼 应：说话者是立法支持者，强调租金暴涨的「毁灭性」影响，devastating effect（毁灭性 的影响）搭配与感情色彩双双贴合。

analysis.label: 竞争词
analysis.text: C) constituent constituent 作形容词意为「组成的」，与 effect 不搭 constituent 虽有形容词用法（组成的、构成整体的），但 constituent effect 不是英语搭配； 其名词义「选民」也与本空语法槽（名词前的定语形容词）语义不合。

questions.stem: his landlord __(31)__ him that his rent was going to go up by $600 a month

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: his landlord 后缺谓语，且后接双宾 him + that 从句，需及物动词过去式

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: notify sb that… 「通知某人……」，房东通知涨租正是此场景 He was leaving our community because his landlord __(31)__ him that his rent was going to go up by $600 a month.——他要搬离，因为房东「通知」他月租要涨 600 美 元。notify sb that 从句句型严丝合缝，因果链（被通知涨租 被迫搬走）完全通顺。

questions.stem: The association __(32)__ that the policy won't actually solve the problem of rental prices.

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: 单数主语 The association 后缺谓语，需三单动词接 that 从句

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: assert that… 「坚称」，正是机构表态反对的措辞 The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposes the legislation. The association __(32)__ that the policy won't actually solve the problem of rental prices. ——协会反对立法，「坚称」该政策解决不了租金问题。assert 接 that 从句表强硬主张， 与前句 opposes 的反对立场无缝衔接。

analysis.label: 竞争词
analysis.text: H) entails entail 是及物动词接名词性成分，不接 that 从句 entails 意为「使必要、涉及」，用法是 A entails B（B 为名词/动名词），如 The job entails travel；它没有 entail that 从句表「声称」的用法，代入后句法不成立。

analysis.label: 易错
analysis.text: 最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— entails 与 asserts 同为三单，形态零区分度，最易凭模糊 词义选错。The association __(32)__ that the policy won't actually solve the problem of rental prices. 中 entails 词性、时态全部合格，「涉及问题」的字面意思又和语境沾边， 是最强干扰。防坑口诀：空后是 that 从句时先问动词能不能带宾语从句——entail 只能接 名词性宾语，assert 才能接 that 从句表「坚称」，句法门槛一过见分晓。

questions.stem: The rent control policy has failed everywhere it has been __(33)__ in this county.

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: has been 之后需过去分词，构成现在完成被动语态

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: 法律政策「被颁布实施」用 enact，法案语域的专属动词 The rent control policy has failed everywhere it has been __(33)__ in this county.—— 租金管控政策「凡是在本县被实施过的地方都失败了」。enact 专用于「颁布法律、实施 政策」，与 policy 构成最自然的被动搭配，也是说话者（反对派）论证政策无效的语义 所需。

analysis.label: 竞争词
analysis.text: K) notified notify 的对象是人，政策不能被「通知」 notified 意为「被通知」，其逻辑主语必须是人（sb be notified of/that…）；it 指 policy （物），「政策被通知」语义不通。

questions.stem: It has not fixed one housing problem __(34)__.

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: 句子主干完整（It has not fixed one housing problem），空在句尾作状语，需副词

analysis.label: 依据
analysis.text: 否定句 + anywhere = 「在任何地方都不」，承接上句 everywhere The rent control policy has failed everywhere it has been __(33)__ in this county. It has not fixed one housing problem __(34)__.——上句说政策「处处失败」，本句递进 「它在任何地方都没能解决哪怕一个住房问题」。not…anywhere 是英语否定的标准搭配， 与 everywhere 形成语义对仗，语气一气呵成。

analysis.label: 竞争词
analysis.text: L) notwithstanding notwithstanding 表让步「尽管如此」，与本句递进逻辑冲突 notwithstanding 作副词意为「尽管如此」（表让步转折），而本句与上句是递进强调（处处失 败 一个问题都没解决），不是让步；且 notwithstanding 通常不单独置于句尾修饰否定陈述 句，代入后逻辑和句法双不通。

analysis.label: 词性槽
analysis.text: when 引导的省略状语从句 when (it is) doing，需现在分词

analysis.label: 依据

A) For those "citizens of the world", the office can be anything from a beach hut in Brisbane to a Starbucks in Seattle, thanks to the growing prevalence of remote-based work. But roaming the globe from café to café is not without its challenges.
B) When the average traveller lands in a city like Bangkok, Berlin, or Buenos Aires, their first step might be to drop their bags at their hotel and to log on to TripAdvisor to find out the hours of a popular tourist attraction or the best rooftop bar for happy hour.
C) But people like Pieter Levels are not your average traveller. A Dutch website developer, Levels has been living and working nomadically(像游牧民那样) in places like Singapore, Hong Kong, Tokyo and Manila for two years. With just a carry-on backpack, he chooses his location at will, based on a variety of factors—Wi-Fi speed, average temperature, exotic food and cost of living—that have little bearing on the work he actually does.
D) Somewhere in his nomadic journey, Levels noticed that there was a growing need to create an online infrastructure for people like himself. That's when he created #nomads, a membership-based chat system which runs on the team communication platform known as Slack. The channel allows users to ask people in their current city the types of practical questions that a tourist would unlikely need to ask.
E) Members of the geographically dispersed subculture that Levels is a part of call themselves "digital nomads". They are borderless, mostly self-employed remote workers who interact with cities in a way that's entirely different from a tourist, but still doesn't quite reach the status of resident. A relatively new phenomenon, there are no hard statistics on the prevalence of digital nomads or location independent workers. But thanks to the growing prevalence of freelance(自由职业的) livelihoods, a global sharing economy and numerous digital tools, the number of people who are able to live this life is growing quickly. And in a rapidly urbanising world, where a major city in Asia increasingly offers the same comforts as one in Europe, many people are reaching the realisation they don't need to stay in one place.
F) So how does a nomad differ from a tourist or resident? In many ways, Levels says, you can think of a digital nomad like a "short-term independent expat(移居国外的人)". Unlike a resident expat, they don't work for a large multinational company in an air conditioned office building and they generally enter a country on a tourist visa, simply renewing or moving on when it expires. But unlike a tourist, they don't arrive in a foreign city without any responsibilities. Travel isn't necessarily required for them to do their jobs, but neither is staying in one place.
G) Janet Brent is an independent ebook designer. She says many people she knows assume she travels for work, but in reality her international destinations are largely up to her, and driven by cost. "Contrary to what some people might think, I don't get paid to travel—I simply choose the lifestyle. Rather than rent in one given city, I choose to travel and do short-term, temporary stays around the world, and my travel decisions are literally based on what makes the most sense financially for me," Brent said. "It's completely different from vacationing—you really sink into the city life and get your feet wet in the communities."
H) Bryce Adams is another such nomad. He works as a developer for a South African company WooThemes, which has a workforce that's more than 80% remote-based. Though Adams frequently posts pictures on Instagram of his enviable cooking adventures from Seoul to Bangkok, he says nomad life in foreign cities has its downsides, including finding adequate Wi-Fi for the bandwidth- hungry work his livelihood depends on. Contrary to the perception that he works under a mango tree in a tropical haven, Adams says the reality of this life means that he often ends up staying in more western style places in globalised cities—ones that are sure to have air conditioning and a decent connection—rather than exotic beachfront cafés.
I) "A fellow nomad posted quite a funny but honest message on Twitter a few days ago that stuck with me: 'It's funny that digital nomads spend 16 hours to fly to the other side of the world to sit in Starbucks,' and it's completely true," Adams said. "When you're a digital nomad, you don't actually have as much freedom as most people think you do. We have deadlines, we all have people relying on us and a mouth (or two) that needs to be fed. It's nice to be able to work anywhere in the world but it's not without its challenges."
J) But these challenges can often provide an opportunity for nomads to see a side of a city they may not have if they were staying in a luxury hotel for a long weekend. However inconvenient, a trip to a local doctor, immigration office or laundry—or a conflict with a local Airbnb host (the accommodation style of choice for most nomads)—can be far more culturally instructive than a trip to the national museum. And because nomads often have to stay where the strongest internet connection is, they tend to spend more time in developing cities compared to the average tourist, who often flees to more touristy destinations soon after landing at the airport.
K) The nomad life is, by all accounts, one built out of privilege. You not only need a relatively powerful passport that makes tourist visas easy to attain, but also a knowledge economy job and access to the technology and devices that make remote working possible. But nomads like Adams say that while they are aware of this privilege, they believe living this way elevates what they're able to offer, by giving them a broader perspective on what they're building, writing, or designing and expanding their world view.
L) "Being able to travel and get around makes it easy to stay inspired," he added. "I truly believe that it makes me a more sensible human being, as I tend to see and appreciate the creative solutions people come up with in other parts of the world, even though many tend to have far more constraints than we have at home."
M) So when you're constantly on the road and don't own any property or have a fixed address, which city do you call home? It's no surprise that many nomads are dual citizens or "third culture kids," who have grown up with a notion of identity that's not tied to nationalism or staying in one place. Levels says that the nomad life has not only changed his notions of citizenship, but the people he chooses to spend time with as well. "Saying you're a 'citizen of the world' is a super cliché, right? But it's becoming quite true," Levels said. "This global awareness has been the reason I started Nomad List and it's affected who my friends are. It's normal to have dinner now and sit with a Korean girl, a British-Singaporean guy, a Mexican girl and a Nigerian guy. As much as that sounds like a politically correct TV advertisement, it's great that that's the time we're in now."

P1 About a decade ago, the G-20, a forum of the world's biggest economies, agreed to crack down on multinational corporations' abusive use of tax havens. This resulted in a plan that aimed to curb practices that shielded a large chunk of corporate profits from tax authorities.

P2 But, instead of reining in the use of tax havens—countries such as the Bahamas and Cayman Islands with very low or no effective tax rates—the problem has only gotten worse.

P3 In a new study, we measured the excessive profits reported in tax havens that cannot be explained by ordinary economic activity such as employees, factories and research in that country. Our findings show a striking pattern of artificial shifting of paper profits to tax havens by corporations, which has been relentless since the 1980s. Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.

P4 We found that the world's biggest multinational businesses shifted 37% of the profits—$969 billion—they earned in other countries to tax havens in 2019. The figure was less than 2% in the 1970s. The main reasons for the large increase were the growth of the tax avoidance industry in the 1980s and U.S. policies that made it easier to shift profits from high-tax countries to tax havens.

P5 We estimate that the amount of corporate taxes lost as a result reached 10% of total corporate revenue in 2019, up from less than 0.1% in the 1970s. In 2019, the total government tax loss globally was $250 billion. U.S. multinational corporations alone accounted for about half of that, followed by the U.K. and Germany.

P6 How do policymakers fix this? So far, the world as a whole has been trying to solve this problem by cutting or scrapping corporate taxes in a very gradual way. In the past 40 years, the global effective corporate tax rate has fallen from 23% to 17%. At the same time, governments have relied more heavily on consumption taxes.

P7 But the root cause of profit-shifting is the incentives involved, such as generous or lenient corporate tax rates in other countries. If countries could agree on a global minimum corporate tax rate of, say, 20%, the problem of profit-shifting would largely disappear, as tax havens would simply cease to exist.

P8 This type of mechanism is exactly what more than 130 countries signed onto in 2021, with implementation of a 15% minimum tax set to begin soon in the EU, U.K., Japan, Indonesia and many other countries. The U.S. has notably not been able to pass this legislation.

P9 Our research suggests implementing this type of tax reform is necessary in reversing the shift of ever-greater amounts of corporate profits to tax havens—instead of being taxed by the governments where they operate and create value.

P1 Children's use of social media is a problem. That doesn't mean it should be stopped. While younger children should not be on platforms where 13 is the minimum age, it is neither practical nor desirable to imagine a world in which teenagers are prevented from accessing the platforms and messaging systems that the adults around them use to organise their lives.

P2 But the pleasure and stimulation that people of all ages find on their screens and smartphones must not blind us to the harm that spending time in this way can cause. The finding that the alarmingly high rate of depression in British teenage girls is closely correlated to time spent on social media is extremely concerning. Research found that two in five girls are on social media for at least three hours a day—with half as many boys engaged to the same extent. More than a third of depressed girls have experienced online harassment. About half of affected girls suffered disrupted sleep, compared with 20% of depressed boys. Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.

P3 Although the research does not prove that social media causes depression, the importance of the finding that there is a connection should not be underestimated. Schools have done important work in communicating key messages about the risks of online abuse. But when it comes to broader questions about "screen time", many professionals as well as parents are confused and uncertain.

P4 The health secretary, Matt Hancock, wants official guidelines on time and age limits. This idea has the virtue of simplicity, though some experts question its effects and call for a greater degree of differentiation, arguing that time online by itself is not a bad thing and it all depends on what you are doing. Also due this year is information commissioner Elizabeth Denham's Age Appropriate Design Code, covering the use of children's personal data. Both initiatives are welcome. But the government is playing catch-up. Statutory regulation of the digital media giants is long overdue. The failure to protect children from data harvesting and targeted advertising thus far is as shocking as the lack of concern shown by the companies themselves with regard to children's psychological health.

P5 Of course, social media companies are not the source of all our ills, and can offer a too-easy target for politicians keen to divert attention from inadequately resourced schools and health services. There are other reasons for the rising incidence of depression in young people, with increasing pressure to succeed in education and in life more broadly—to be famous, beautiful, rich—often cited as a source of unhappiness or anxiety which can, if aggravated by other factors and not managed, tip into ill health. Safeguarding means more than the avoidance of physical threat.

writing.model: With the trend of Urbanization, it is vitally important for city residents to develop a stronger love for Nature. As concrete forests expand, many urban dwellers rarely feel the breeze, hear birds, or touch soil. A stronger bond with nature is not a luxury; it is essential for mental and physical well-being in an increasingly artificial environment. One practical way to cultivate this love is to make nature part of daily routines. For example, residents can walk in nearby parks, grow plants on balconies, or join community gardening projects. These activities reconnect people with the living world. Last year, I started visiting a small riverbank park every weekend. Watching seasons change there reduced my stress and made me more aware of environmental protection. Therefore, city governments and individuals should work together to create more green spaces and spend time in them. Only by integrating nature into urban life can residents truly develop a stronger love for it and build healthier cities for future generations.

translation.source: 科技进步使中国的医疗事业得到快速发展。近年来，远程医疗使优质医疗资源惠及更多患者。医学专家可以通过视频为偏远地区患者提供咨询，指导当地医生制定并实施治疗方案。人工智能辅助诊断系统帮助医生识别患者的早期症状，提高诊断准确率。电子健康档案的普及让医生能够快速了解患者病史，避免重复检查。线上医疗咨询平台极大地方便了患者就诊。科技与医疗的深度融合更好地满足了人民的健康需求。
translation.reference: Advances in science and technology have brought about the rapid development of China's medical services. In recent years, telemedicine has made high-quality medical resources accessible to more patients. Through video links, medical experts can provide consultations for patients in remote areas, guiding local doctors in developing and implementing treatment plans. AI-assisted diagnosis systems help doctors identify patients' early symptoms, thereby improving the accuracy of diagnosis. The widespread adoption of electronic health records enables doctors to quickly review patients' medical histories, thus avoiding repeated examinations. Online medical consultation platforms have also greatly facilitated patients' access to medical care. Overall, the deep integration of technology and healthcare has better met people's health needs.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 科技进步作主语，带来作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 科技进步使中国的医疗事业得到快速发展的核心动作是「使……得到快速发展」，提主干为 Advances in science and technology（主语）+ have brought about（谓语）+ the rapid development of China's medical services（宾语）；「中国的医疗事业」整体降为宾语内部的修 饰成分。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「使……得到发展」并入一个及物动词 「使中国的医疗事业得到快速发展」不宜逐字译成 make China's medical services get developed（典型中式英语），把「快速发展」做成名词短语 the rapid development of China's medical services 作宾语，用一个及物动词 brought about（带来）即可完整承载「使……得到」 的因果语义。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 得到快速发展表示已发生且延续至今的结果，此处偏离全篇一般现在时的基调，改用现在完成时 have brought about；若用一般现在时 brings about，会丢掉「已然实现」的意味。 主谓一致 主语中心词 advances 是复数，助动词用 have，不要误写为 has。 冠词与单复数 development 被 of China's medical services 限定为特指，前面加 the；medical services 用复 数表医疗服务的统称。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Advances in science and technology have brought about the rapid development of China's medical services. 2. 近年来，远程医疗使优质医疗资源惠及更多患者。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 远程医疗作主语，使资源可及作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 远程医疗使优质医疗资源惠及更多患者的主语「远程医疗」照搬为 telemedicine；「使优质医疗资 源惠及更多患者」用英文惯用复合宾语结构 has made high-quality medical resources accessible to more patients——「惠及」没有一个逐字对应的英文动词，make sth accessible to sb 是地道对译。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「近年来」降为时间状语前置 本句主干之外只有近年来一个成分，译为时间状语 In recent years 置于句首，既符合英文把时间 状语放句首标示话题的习惯，又天然起到承接上句的作用；句内其余部分无需再降级。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「近年来」标示从过去持续到现在，是现在完成时的典型信号，用 has made；这是基调时态的合 理偏离。 主谓一致 主语 telemedicine 是不可数单数，助动词用 has，不要受中文无单复数标记影响写成 have。 单复数 「优质医疗资源」「更多患者」均为复数概念：high-quality medical resources、more patients，patients 不要漏掉 s。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: In recent years, telemedicine has made high-quality medical resources accessible to more patients. 3. 医学专家可以通过视频为偏远地区患者提供咨询，指导当地医生制定并实施治疗方案。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 医学专家作主语，提供咨询作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 医学专家可以通过视频为偏远地区患者提供咨询给出明确主语「医学专家」→medical experts， 谓语取「提供咨询」→can provide consultations；后半句指导当地医生制定并实施治疗方案不另 立谓语，留给降级处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 方式状语前置，伴随动作分词化 「通过视频」 介词短语 Through video links 作方式状语置句首；「为偏远地区患者」→for patients in remote areas，其中「偏远地区」用介词短语 in remote areas 作 patients 的后置定 语，不堆在名词前；「指导当地医生制定并实施治疗方案」 现在分词短语 guiding local doctors in developing and implementing treatment plans 作伴随状语，「制定并实施」在 guide sb in doing sth 框架内用 and 连接两个动名词。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态与情态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时，can 后接动词原形 provide；本句陈述的是当下的能力，不用完成 时。 介词搭配 provide sth for sb（为某人提供某物）与 guide sb in doing sth（指导某人做某事）是固定搭 配，介词 for／in 不可换、不可省。 单复数 consultations、treatment plans 均用复数表泛指的一类；experts、doctors 复数与中文「专家 们／医生们」的群体义一致。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Through video links, medical experts can provide consultations for patients in remote areas, guiding local doctors in developing and implementing treatment plans. 4. 人工智能辅助诊 断系统帮助医生识别患者的早期症状，提高诊断准确率。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 诊断系统作主语，帮助识别作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 人工智能辅助诊 断系统帮助医生识别患者的早期症状主语照搬为 AI-assisted diagnosis systems （systems 复数表一类事物），谓语用 help sb do 结构：help doctors identify patients' early symptoms；「识别」紧跟 help 用原形。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「提高准确率」降为结果状语 提高诊断准确率是「帮助识别早期症状」带来的结果，译为 thereby improving the accuracy of diagnosis 作结果状语挂句尾；「诊断准确率」不直译为 diagnosis correct rate（中式），用 the accuracy of diagnosis 这个名词化表达。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 陈述系统的一般功能，回指全篇基调用一般现在时 help。 动词用法 help 后接不带 to 的不定式：help doctors identify（to identify 也算对，但 identify 更简洁）； 不要误写 help doctors identifying。 单复数 systems、doctors、symptoms 均用复数；symptoms 最易漏 s，注意「患者的早期症状」是多 个症状。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: AI-assisted diagnosis systems help doctors identify patients' early symptoms, thereby improving the accuracy of diagnosis. 5. 电子健康档案的普及让医生能够快速了解患 者病史，避免重复检查。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 普及作主语，使医生能够作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 电子健康档案的普及是「动词＋的＋名词」结构，译成名词化短语 The widespread adoption of electronic health records 作整句主语；「让医生能够」用 enable sb to do：enables doctors to quickly review patients' medical histories。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「避免重复检查」降为结果状语 避免重复检查是「快速了解病史」的直接结果，用 thus avoiding repeated examinations 作结果 状语挂句尾；「让」译作 enable sb to do 已含「能够」义，「能够」不再另译 can，避免 enable...to be able to 的冗余。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 主谓一致 主语中心词是 adoption（单数），不是 records，谓语用 enables——长主语里隔着 of 短语时， 最容易被末尾的复数名词带偏。 时态 陈述现实功能，回指基调用一般现在时。 单复数 records、histories 用复数；「病史」也可作 a patient's medical history，两种译法取一即可， 全篇保持可数名词标记完整。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The widespread adoption of electronic health records enables doctors to quickly review patients' medical histories, thus avoiding repeated examinations. 6. 线上医疗咨询平台极大地方便了患者就诊。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 平台作主语，方便就诊作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 线上医疗咨询平台极大地方便了患者就诊主语照搬为 Online medical consultation platforms； 「方便了患者就诊」不逐字译 convenient for patients to see doctors（中式且破碎），用 facilitate ＋名词化宾语：have greatly facilitated patients' access to medical care。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「极大地」作副词修饰谓语 本句结构简单，无需降级：「极大地」 副词 greatly 直接修饰谓语动词；「患者就诊」名词化为 patients' access to medical care 作宾语，access to 是固定搭配。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「方便了」表已成事实且影响延续，偏离基调用现在完成时 have facilitated。 主谓一致与单复数 主语 platforms 复数，助动词用 have；platforms 的 s 不可漏。 介词搭配 access to 中的 to 是介词固定搭配，不可换成 for 或 of。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Online medical consultation platforms have greatly facilitated patients' access to medical care. 7. 科技与医疗的深度融合更好地满足了人民的健康需求。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 深度融合作主语，满足需求作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 科技与医疗的深度融合译成名词化主语 The deep integration of technology and healthcare （integration 为中心词）；谓语「满足了」→has met；宾语人民的健康需求→people's health needs，needs 用复数。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「更好地」作副词嵌入谓语 本句为简单句，无成分需降级：「更好地」→better 置于助动词与过去分词之间（has better met），修饰「满足」的程度。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 主谓一致 主语中心词 integration 是单数，助动词用 has；不要被 of 后面的 technology and healthcare 两个名词带成 have。 时态 「更好地满足了」呼应全篇「已经实现的成果」，用现在完成时 has met，与首句 have brought about 首尾呼应。 单复数 「健康需求」是多种需求，needs 用复数；meet one's needs 为固定搭配。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The deep integration of technology and healthcare has better met people's health needs. 英语六级 2026年6月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
